messages:
eli: FYI I opened PR #981 to update the SDK snippets for cursor-based pagination + streaming retries. The current docs show page-number style examples which are confusing. Need a tiny canonical set for py/ts/go and a quick CI snippet test.

nina: I can take python and the migration note. Prefer showing how to resume a streaming request using the cursor token (very short). Also saw a broken link from /docs/streaming -> /docs/streaming-old. I'll patch that in the PR.

eli: Great. Keep the python snippet sync-generator style and mention idempotency concerns. Example idea (short):
```python
# resume-able streaming (sync)
def stream_resume(client, prompt, cursor=None):
    for chunk in client.generate_stream(prompt, cursor=cursor):
        yield chunk
```

omar: I'll do TS async iterator and a one-liner backoff helper inline so readers don't need extra imports. Quick draft: 
```ts
// resume + retry (async)
async function streamResume(client, prompt, cursor){
  for await (const c of client.generateStream({prompt, cursor})) console.log(c.text)
}
```

nina: For Go, show receiving loop + note about passing ctx with deadline. Make sure snippets are <= 10 lines for runner.

ci-bot: snippet-check triggered -> found one docs snippet with triple-backtick fence inside a fenced block causing build failure in markdown parser. File: examples/streams.md line ~42. Suggest use indented block or remove nested fences.

eli: Thanks @ci-bot. I'll fix the nested fence and push a tiny test that executes each snippet with mocked client so CI catches runtime regressions.

omar: Also: add a short sentence in migration.md explaining cursor semantics (cursor points to last-committed token; resume is best-effort).

eli: Ok assigning reviewers @nina @omar. Plan: land link fix + snippet updates + CI test in one PR, then backfill other references. Merge after snippet-check passes.
